10950-the-mirror-of-literature-amusement.title: The Mirror Of Literature Amusement And Instruction Volume 13
10950-the-mirror-of-literature-amusement.creator: Unknown
10950-the-mirror-of-literature-amusement.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The offices are spread out, like the villas of the ancients, upon the ground-floor. Adjoining the front of the villa is a tent-like canopy, surmounting a spacious apartment, set aside, we believe, for splendid _dejeuné_ entertainments in the summer. This roof may be seen from several parts of the park.

arxiv-1612-00622.title: Blow-up lemmas for sparse graphs HH was supported by the FONDECYT Iniciación grant 11150913 and by Millenium Nucleus Information and Coordination in Networks. YK was supported by FAPESP (2013/03447-6) and CNPq (459335/2014-6, 310974/2013-5). YP was partially supported by DFG grant PE 2299/1-1. The c
arxiv-1612-00622.creator: Peter Allen, Julia Böttcher, Hiệp Hàn, Yoshiharu Kohayakawa, Yury Person
arxiv-1612-00622.description: Abstract . The blow-up lemma states that a system of super-regular pairs contains all bounded degree spanning graphs as subgraphs that embed into a corresponding system of complete pairs. This lemma has far-reaching applications in extremal combinatorics. We prove sparse analogues of the blow-up lemma for subgraphs of random and of pseudorandom graphs.

arxiv-1909-02407.title: Linking Zonal Winds and Gravity: The Relative Importance of Dynamic Self Gravity
arxiv-1909-02407.creator: J. Wicht, W. Dietrich, P. Wulff, U. R. Christensen
arxiv-1909-02407.description: Abstract Recent precise measurements at Jupiter’s and Saturn’s gravity fields constrain the properties of the zonal flows in the outer envelopes of these planets. A simplified dynamic equation, sometimes called the thermal wind or thermo-gravitational wind equation, establishes a link between zonal flows and the related buoyancy perturbation, which in turn can be exploited to yield the dynamic gravity perturbation.

arxiv-2007-06571.title: Inverse Cubic Iteration
arxiv-2007-06571.creator: Robert M. Corless
arxiv-2007-06571.description: Abstract There are thousands of papers on rootfinding for nonlinear scalar equations. Here is one more, to talk about an apparently new method, which I call “Inverse Cubic Iteration” (ICI) in analogy to the Inverse Quadratic Iteration in Richard Brent’s zeroin method. The possibly new method is based on a cubic blend of tangent-line approximations for the inverse function.

arxiv-2012-06700.title: Planetesimal formation around the snow line. II. Dust or pebbles?
arxiv-2012-06700.creator: Ryuki Hyodo, Tristan Guillot, Shigeru Ida, Satoshi Okuzumi, Andrew N. Youdin
arxiv-2012-06700.description: Abstract Context. Forming planetesimals is a major challenge in our current understanding of planet formation. Around the snow line, icy pebbles and silicate dust may locally pile up and form icy and rocky planetesimals via a streaming instability and/or gravitational instability.

arxiv-2203-12947.title: Diffusivity dependence of the transition path ensemble
arxiv-2203-12947.creator: Lukas Kikuchi, Ronojoy Adhikari, Julian Kappler
arxiv-2203-12947.description: Abstract At low temperatures transition pathways of stochastic dynamical systems are typically approximated by instantons. Here we show, using a dynamical system containing two competing pathways, that even at low-to-intermediate temperatures, instantons can fail to capture the most likely transition pathway.

arxiv-2206-12205.title: Bits missing: Finding exotic pulsars using bfloat16 on NVIDIA GPUs
arxiv-2206-12205.creator: Jack White, Karel Adámek, Jayanta Roy, Sofia Dimoudi, Scott M. Ransom, Wesley Armour
arxiv-2206-12205.description: Abstract The Fourier Domain Acceleration Search (FDAS) is an effective technique for detecting faint binary pulsars in large radio astronomy datasets. This paper quantifies the sensitivity impact of reducing numerical precision in the GPU accelerated FDAS pipeline of the AstroAccelerate software package.

arxiv-2210-08676.title: Scale-Agnostic Super-Resolution in MRI using Feature-Based Coordinate Networks
arxiv-2210-08676.creator: Dave Van Veen, Rogier van der Sluijs, Batu Ozturkler, Arjun Desai, Christian Bluethgen, Robert D. Boutin, Marc H. Willis, Gordon Wetzstein, David Lindell, Shreyas Vasanawala, John Pauly, Akshay S. Chaudhari
arxiv-2210-08676.description: Abstract We propose using a coordinate network decoder for the task of super-resolution in MRI. The continuous signal representation of coordinate networks enables this approach to be scale-agnostic, i.e. one can train over a continuous range of scales and subsequently query at arbitrary resolutions.

arxiv-2303-08332.title: Electron wave functions in beta-decay formulas revisited (II): Completion including recoil-order and induced currents
arxiv-2303-08332.creator: Wataru Horiuchi, Toru Sato, Yuichi Uesaka, Kenichi Yoshida
arxiv-2303-08332.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wataru Horiuchi, Toru Sato, Yuichi Uesaka, Kenichi Yoshida. We present complete formulas of the allowed and first-forbidden transitions of the nuclear beta decay taking into account the recoil-order and induced currents up to the next-to-leading order (NLO). The longitudinal part of the vector current is cleared away by the use of the conservation of the vector current for the multipole operators of the natural-parity transitions, which makes the effect of the meson exchange current for the vector current as small as possible.

arxiv-2408-10001.title: Coprime Bivariate Bicycle Codes and Their Layouts on Cold Atoms
arxiv-2408-10001.creator: Ming Wang, Frank Mueller
arxiv-2408-10001.description: Abstract Quantum computing is deemed to require error correction at scale to mitigate physical noise by reducing it to lower noise levels while operating on encoded logical qubits. Popular quantum error correction schemes include CSS code, of which surface codes provide regular mappings onto 2D planes suitable for contemporary quantum devices together with known transversal logical gates.

arxiv-2410-21437.title: Revisiting Fekete’s Lemma, Subadditive and Periodic Sequences
arxiv-2410-21437.creator: Angshuman R. Goswami
arxiv-2410-21437.description: Abstract . In this paper, we present an alternative proof of Fekete’s Lemma. We demonstrate that for any subadditive sequence, it is possible to construct a subadditive function that exactly interpolates the sequence. Using this result, along with Hille’s theorem on subadditive functions, we naturally arrive at Fekete’s Lemma.

arxiv-2502-16978.title: Pinch-line spin liquids as layered Coulomb phases and applications to cubic models
arxiv-2502-16978.creator: N. Davier, F. A. Gómez Albarracín, H. Diego Rosales, P. Pujol, Ludovic D.C. Jaubert
arxiv-2502-16978.description: Abstract Spin liquids form fluctuating magnetic textures which have to obey certain rules imposed by frustration. These rules can often be written in the form of a Gauss law, indicating the local conservation of an emergent electric field. In reciprocal space, these emergent Gauss laws appear as singularities known as pinch points, that are accessible to neutron-scattering measurements.

arxiv-2507-06329.title: MixAssist: An Audio-Language Dataset for Co-Creative AI Assistance in Music Mixing
arxiv-2507-06329.creator: Michael Clemens & Ana Marasović
arxiv-2507-06329.description: Abstract While AI presents significant potential for enhancing music mixing and mastering workflows, current research predominantly emphasizes end-to-end automation or generation, often overlooking the collaborative and instructional dimensions vital for co-creative processes. This gap leaves artists, particularly amateurs seeking to develop expertise, underserved.

pmc-10735889.title: PATTERNS OF ANTIHYPERTENSIVES CHANGE AND MORTALITY IN VA NURSING HOME RESIDENTS
pmc-10735889.creator: Xiaojuan Liu, Michelle Odden
pmc-10735889.description: Antihypertensive treatment is common in nursing home residents, yet data on the frequency and pattens of treatment changes in this group are lacking. We described the patterns of antihypertensive treatment changes and examined the mortality rate in 24870 Veterans Affairs (VA) nursing home residents ≥65 years with long-term stays (≥180 days) from 2006-2019.

pmc-11554627.title: An intelligent poly aptamer-encoded DNA nanoclew for tumor site activated mitochondria-targeted photodynamic therapy and MR imaging
pmc-11554627.creator: Minghui Chen, Hanbo Xu, Pengzhao Chang, Xueqi Li, Shuang Liu, Lingyue Xu, Kai Xu, Guohui Cheng
pmc-11554627.description: Mitochondria-targeted photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as one of the most promising antitumor therapies, as it significantly enhances the efficacy of photosensitizers. An efficient and biocompatible nanocarrier to deliver cationic photosensitizers (PSs) is vital for mitochondria-targeted PDT but still challenging.

pmc-11712902.title: Importance of digital skills in attitude towards the use of smartphones and usage behavior in ederly population
pmc-11712902.creator: Estela Benitez, Elsa Araceli Revollo Sarmiento, Maria Celeste López Moreno, Rocio Micaela Vera, Leticia Vivas
pmc-11712902.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe use of technology in elderly population has increased in the past years due to COVID‐19. Therefore it is relevant to identify the factors that contribute and limit the effective use of technology by older people. In particular, digital skills have shown to be relevant to determine the attitude toward the use of technology and consequently to have an effect on usage behavior.

pmc-12454494.title: Heart in a knot: unraveling the impact of the nested tori myofiber architecture on ventricular mechanics
pmc-12454494.creator: Kasra Osouli, Francesco De Gaetano, Maria Laura Costantino, Mathias Peirlinck
pmc-12454494.description: The intricate three-dimensional organization of cardiac myofibers and sheetlets plays a critical role in the mechanical behavior of the human heart. Despite extensive research and the development of various rule-based myofiber architecture surrogate models, the precise arrangement of these structures and their impact on cardiac function remain subjects of debate.
